items.title: Avery "Kid" Howard Interview, 1961-05-22
items.q: And then later on we got Handy out there.

ctx.x: Yeah so he would be more famous as a saxophone player then I guess. That's right, he would. The way you say it and everything it looks like. You must have played with somebody else in the 20s, or you say you had some other places, you had your own band.

Yeah, well I played on Bourbon Street in the 30s at 802 for Sam Columbo. It was right across from the paddock. When the paddock was open up, I had been out there playing across the street. Little Sammy Hopkins was on the piano. Charlie, what's his name? Charlie Sylvester was playing the drum. And Chester Lazard was playing the bass. And then later on we got Handy out there. I played there a long time for him. Who's Handy? John Handy, the saxophone player.
Could be other Handys too, you know. There's a many. I'm sorry, I'm sorry.

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-15
items.q: Oh yeah, Howland and I had a band together.

ctx.x: All different fellas. I never had no particular one to play with. Just afternoon I was in town. He called me up, asked me to work and I'd accept the job.
Never worked with Ken Howland? Oh yeah, Howland and I had a band together.

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1963-11-21
items.q: Whose band was it when you were playing at La Vida with Howard and Jim in the band? Whose band was that? It was my band. Your band? Yeah. Yeah, it was my band.

ctx.x: Yeah. What, after La Vida? No. After we left with La Vida,
we had a band together. Whose band was it when you were playing at La Vida with Howard and Jim in the band? Whose band was that? It was my band. Your band? Yeah. Yeah, it was my band.

Can I get back to the early days for a minute? Yeah, sure. When I'm interested in what I die, say in the 20s, how would they get a brass band to bury them there? Would they hire an organized band always over the days? How about band or what?
